blocks.name: bit-membership
blocks.note: Numeric-uint32 and signed-bit-pattern forms are both explicit; bit-pattern forms avoid unnecessary unsigned scalar coercion.

blocks.name: fixed-width-word-composition
blocks.note: Generic and caller-range-proven cross-word shift profiles coexist; known count ranges avoid runtime dispatch.

blocks.name: first-next-set-bit
blocks.note: General first-set-bit, caller-isolated-bit, caller-isolated clear, clear-lowest-bit, and one/two-lane cardinality profiles coexist. Once a hot iterator has isolated lsb, it should reuse that bit both for indexing and for XOR clearing rather than recomputing the lowest-bit relation.

blocks.name: popcount
blocks.note: Exact popcount now has fixed SWAR, upper-lane-distribution, hot high<=10 table, and set-bit-sparsity profiles. Sparse loops keep K and branch-mispredict penalties explicit; use them only when the expected distribution beats the fixed SWAR ledger.

blocks.name: coordinate-decode
blocks.note: Board geometry is configured at initialization; hot row/column decoding uses prepared lookup tables instead of division/modulo.

blocks.name: legal-landing-cell
blocks.note: Initialization may index landing cells by physical column or move slot. If a caller already observed the current landing cell for scoring, legality, or a known-cell transition, playableKnownCell32 reuses that scalar and avoids a second load. Otherwise playableColumn32 remains the direct load+compare form.

blocks.name: winning-line-test
blocks.note: Signed bit-pattern containment is preferred when masks never require unsigned numeric interpretation.

blocks.name: apply-undo-state-transition
blocks.note: Transition profiles include separate-ply, caller-owned-ply, and packed support+ply representations, each with ordinary and known-cell forms where useful. Packed state is selected only when support+rank fits one uint32 and rows fit the 3-bit support field; combined deltas remove duplicate state traffic. Reflection remains support-only via explicit masking.

blocks.name: hash-mix32
blocks.note: Three explicitly costed hash-mix strengths let the application trade bucket avalanche against cycles.

blocks.name: transposition-cache-probe
blocks.note: Caller computes and retains the table index once; probe is a boolean tag hit and replacement reuses the same index.

blocks.name: canonical-reflection-symmetry
blocks.note: Reflection functions continue to consume support-only packed bits. Configured transition state may physically pack support+ply when it fits, but supportFromPackedSupport32 masks rank away before reflection; rank extraction/reinsertion is never part of the reflection primitive.

blocks.name: frontier-antichain-normalization
blocks.note: Frontier normalization now has lane-selected signed profiles and nonempty lazy-compaction variants. Lazy forms leave the accepted prefix untouched and start writes only after the first rejection, replacing the accepted-store count R with moved accepted entries M. Generic profiles remain for empty/unspecialized callers.

blocks.name: residual-transition
blocks.note: Residual transitions support both class-major and action-major prepared-base layouts. Class-major fits fixed-class/varying-action loops; action-major fits the pinned fixed-action/varying-class residual loop. Initialization transpose cost remains explicit.

blocks.name: move-order-selection
blocks.note: Physical-column, move-slot, exact-seven-slot, and scalar-producer profiles coexist. The scalar seven-slot profile removes score-array loads only when score production already has all seven values live and no caller loads/spills them solely to satisfy the selector. Runtime initialization still owns candidate count/order; move-slot indexing remains aligned with transition data.

blocks.name: shared-atomic-claim-release
blocks.note: Atomic release has notifying and no-notify profiles. Polling or externally awakened consumers select atomicReleaseNoNotify32 and pay only the publication store; Atomics.wait users retain atomicRelease32 so wake semantics are not weakened.

blocks.name: shared-queue-enqueue-dequeue
blocks.note: Queue profiles now separate blocking/nonblocking and shared/owned reservation semantics. Owned blocking sides remove the locked reservation RMW while preserving per-slot Atomics.wait/notify and sequence publication/acquisition; returned next positions keep caller reservation state local.

blocks.name: capacity-growth-rehash
blocks.note: Capacity growth keeps allocation and rehash costs explicit. rehashOverwrite32 now performs only migration; new capacity is caller-known from newMask and is not reconstructed/returned by the primitive.
